messages:
tara: Quick note  customer asks: how do we show which service account actually executed work when their front-end proxies impersonate? Console only shows caller project atm.
kevin: That breaks triage. We only tag meter records with the incoming key.
minh: Proposal: auth-proxy emits `X-RW-EXECUTOR: sa:proj/id/name` signed by proxy. Runtime plumbs into traces and optional metric tag `executor`.
olga: Privacy: don't surface cross-org SA names to viewers without permission. Show a locked badge with tooltip and a link to request access.
telemetry-bot: Reminder: new metric dimension requires cardinality review.
kevin: Cardinality mitigation idea: index top-50 executors per org in the TSDB, roll rest into `executor:other`. Also offer a sampled extraction path for full chains for audit.
tara: UX: add a toggle "Group by -> Caller / Executor" in usage table. Default remains Caller. Executor view is behind feature flag and subject to per-user access checks.
minh: Alerts: make alert rules accept `executor` as grouping but default to `caller_project` to avoid noisy pages. Provide opt-in evaluation mode for teams.
olga: Security: proxies must sign header; runtime should validate HMAC + mTLS to prevent spoofing. Reject requests that set header without valid proxy auth.
kevin: Backfill plan: where traces have executor header we can annotate recent metering records read-only; billing ETL must ignore executor unless org opts in.
tara: Rollout: 1) emit signed header behind flag for internal telemetry for 72h, 2) run 30d cardinality sample, 3) enable executor column behind feature flag with privacy gating, 4) expose opt-in alerting.
telemetry-bot: RFC created: "executor-observability-and-privacy"  attach cardinality numbers and cost estimate.
minh: I'll run the uniqueness job and post numbers. If too many unique executors, we'll reduce index N or rely on sampling.
kevin: I'll draft the proxy PR for header + signing. Tara will draft UI mock. Olga to write privacy copy. Ping #eng-oncall if alerts spike during probe. :thumbsup:
